U-pages__guide--00386--sentence--guide-t.evidence_snippet: Through an Equated Monthly Instalment (EMI) — which includes both the principal and the interest together.

U-pages__guide--00387--list_item--li-275.evidence_snippet: Early years: you’re mostly paying interest.

U-pages__guide--00388--list_item--li-276.evidence_snippet: Later years: you’re mostly paying off the loan.

U-pages__guide--00389--list_item--li-277.evidence_snippet: If the rate stays the same, the EMI stays the same. If the rate changes, the EMI or the years may change.

U-pages__guide--00391--sentence--guide-l.evidence_snippet: Depends on if the property is ready to move in or under construction.

U-pages__guide--00392--list_item--li-292.evidence_snippet: Full EMI about one month after first disbursement.

U-pages__guide--00394--list_item--li-297.evidence_snippet: Interest-only (pre-EMI) on what’s disbursed, then full EMI around possession.

U-pages__guide--00417--section--h399.evidence_snippet: Up to what period can you repay?

U-pages__guide--00418--sentence--guide-t.evidence_snippet: Up to 30 years. Age and bank rules often shorten that period. A longer period lowers the EMI and raises the total interest.

U-pages__guide--00420--section--h416.evidence_snippet: What are the types of interest rates?

U-pages__guide--00421--sentence--guide-t.evidence_snippet: Floating rates, which change over time, and fixed rates, which stay the same for a few years.

U-pages__guide--00422--sentence--guide-l.evidence_snippet: Moves with the benchmark over the loan tenure.

U-pages__guide--00423--list_item--li-435.evidence_snippet: External benchmark (often the repo rate) + the bank’s spread

U-pages__guide--00424--list_item--li-436.evidence_snippet: Repo rate resets at least once every 3 months

U-pages__guide--00425--list_item--li-437.evidence_snippet: When the rate goes up, your lender asks how you want to take the extra cost. You can pay a lump sum, raise EMI, extend tenure, or mix these.

U-pages__guide--00426--list_item--li-438.evidence_snippet:

                        Prepayment / foreclosure charges: none on floating home loans under

U-pages__guide--00429--sentence--guide-l.evidence_snippet: Fixed for a set period, then the rate resets.

U-pages__guide--00430--list_item--li-454.evidence_snippet: External benchmark (often the repo rate) + the bank’s spread + a fixed rate premium

U-pages__guide--00431--list_item--li-455.evidence_snippet: Usually fixed for 3 or 5 years, as per the lender

U-pages__guide--00432--list_item--li-456.evidence_snippet: Usually about 1% to 2% higher than floating during the fixed period

U-pages__guide--00439--sentence--p-478.evidence_snippet: You can switch between fixed and floating rates as per the bank’s policy, at the applicable cost.

U-pages__guide--00440--sentence--p-479.evidence_snippet: You can switch between benchmark rates as per the bank’s policy, at the applicable cost.

U-pages__guide--00441--sentence--p-480.evidence_snippet: If your credit score improves, you can ask to lower your rate as per the bank’s policy, at the applicable cost.

U-pages__guide--00442--sentence--p-481.evidence_snippet: When the repo rate changes, a floating rate must reset within 3 months. Your bank’s reset date sets the exact wait.

U-pages__guide--00446--section--h502.evidence_snippet: What are the types of loan structures?

U-pages__guide--00447--sentence--guide-t.evidence_snippet: A regular term loan or an overdraft (where spare cash reduces interest).

U-pages__guide--00448--sentence--guide-l.evidence_snippet: This is the normal home loan. You pay a fixed EMI every month, and interest is charged on the unpaid loan balance. Money in your savings account does not change that.

U-pages__guide--00449--list_item--li-521.evidence_snippet: To cut interest early, you have to prepay

U-pages__guide--00450--list_item--li-522.evidence_snippet: Fits if you will not keep large surplus parked for months

U-pages__guide--00452--sentence--guide-l.evidence_snippet: This home loan is linked to an account. When spare cash sits in that account, interest is charged on a lower balance. You can still withdraw that money when you need it.

U-pages__guide--00453--list_item--li-530.evidence_snippet: Rate is usually 0.15% to 1% higher than the same bank’s term loan

U-pages__guide--00454--list_item--li-531.evidence_snippet: You benefit only if parked surplus saves more interest than the higher rate costs

U-pages__guide--00460--sentence--p-552.evidence_snippet: You can switch between term loan and overdraft later as per the bank’s policy, at the applicable cost.

U-pages__guide--00461--sentence--p-553.evidence_snippet: On overdraft, withdrawing parked money follows the bank’s limit and rules.

U-pages__guide--00462--sentence--p-554.evidence_snippet: On overdraft, the usable limit may fall over the years (dropline), as per the lender.

U-pages__home-loan-complaints--00187--se.evidence_snippet: Shroffin is not a bank, a Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC), or a lender. We do not approve, sanction, underwrite, or disburse loans. The lender decides your rate, your fees, and whether you are approved.

U-pages__home-loan-complaints--00188--se.evidence_snippet: Even so, we try our best for you. We show each lender's home loan clearly, one next to the other.

U-pages__home-loan-complaints--00190--se.evidence_snippet: We take each lender's terms and check them with that lender. Then we put the home loans next to each other, so you can compare. We can also help you apply.

U-pages__home-loan-complaints--00191--se.evidence_snippet: The rates and rules we show can change. The ones the lender gives you can be different. That still depends on your credit, income, documents, the property, and the checks the lender makes. Some of this may not apply to you, to your city, or when you apply.

U-pages__home-loan-complaints--00192--se.evidence_snippet: Seeing a lender does not mean they will lend to you. We cannot make a lender say yes, or take back a no. When they answer, we go through it with you, and we help you decide what to do. You still choose. What the lender writes is what counts.

U-pages__home-loan-complaints--00193--se.evidence_snippet: If you take the loan, the agreement is with the lender, not with us. We do not become your lender. Read the sanction letter, the key fact statement, and the loan documents before you accept.

U-privacy-policy--00119--list_item--li-4.evidence_snippet: withdraw consent where processing is based on consent;

U-privacy-policy--00121--list_item--li-4.evidence_snippet: nominate another person to exercise rights on your behalf where the law provides for nomination;

U-privacy-policy--00122--list_item--li-4.evidence_snippet: complain to the Data Protection Board of India once that channel is available for your case.
